blocks.content: Lines of latitude are called parallels because they maintain an equal distance from one another and never intersect.

rows: Converge and intersect at the Poles
Only Equator is a Great Circle
All pairs of opposite meridians form Great Circles

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Parallels of latitude are imaginary concentric circles drawn parallel to the Equator running in an east-west direction.
Unlike meridians of longitude, lines of latitude remain at a constant distance from each other and never intersect.
The linear distance between each degree of latitude is constant across the globe at approximately 111 kilometres (69 miles).
The Equator is the longest parallel and the only line of latitude that forms a Great Circle.
The circumference of latitude circles progressively decreases from the Equator toward the poles, where they shrink to single points.
Direct questions often ask for the distance between two degrees of latitude (111 km or 69 miles).
Crucial distinction: All meridians of longitude are equal in length, whereas parallels of latitude decrease in length from the Equator to the Poles.
Only the Equator (0°) is a Great Circle among all parallels; all other parallels are Small Circles.
